sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Non-Vessel Operating Common Carrier (NVOCC) Ocean Box Brokerage

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental European, French-influenced code-based system; sources include the Civil Code, Commercial Companies Law of 10 August 1915, and administrative regulations)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) investment protection framework
Luxembourg-China Agreement on the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (in force)
Luxembourg-China Double Taxation Agreement (1979 DTA, as amended by the Protocol signed 6 November 2014)
Luxembourg-United States Double Taxation Treaty (1996, as amended by the 2009 Protocol)
EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (CAI) - concluded in principle on 30 December 2020; ratification suspended; not yet in force

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (SCSp regime at articles 22-1 to 22-11, inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and amending the Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (2004 AML Law), as further amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 and the Law of 3 June 2021; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 14 July 2019 on RBE procedures and fees; CSSF Regulation 12-02 on AML/CFT professional obligations; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) as amended by the Law of 17 May 2022 reorganizing the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); Law of 2 September 2011 on access to regulated professions (autorisation d'établissement)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and current registry extract of the corporate shareholder/general partner (e.g. Chinese parent company, valid copy issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation - SAMR)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation of the People's Republic of China (SAMR)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille - Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC (Apostille Convention in force for China since 7 November 2023); if the certificate is used in a non-Hague counterparty state, full consular legalization by the Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate applies as fallback

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (certificate of existence and no default) of the corporate shareholder/general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation of the People's Republic of China (SAMR) or competent Chinese notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via notarization by Chinese notary and PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs; alternate route for non-Hague jurisdictions: consular legalization through Luxembourg diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate authorization: board resolution or equivalent approving the incorporation of the Luxembourg SCSp, appointment of the initial general partner, and designation of signatory authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or board of directors of the shareholder/general partner company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in jurisdiction of origin and Hague Apostille (PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Chinese corporate deeds); translation into French or English by a sworn/certified translator acceptable to LBR and the Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) and the future managers of the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of residence of each UBO (China: Chinese notary with apostille; Luxembourg: Luxembourg notary upon original passport inspection)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for documents notarized in China or other Contracting States; consular legalization only if the UBO is resident in a non-Hague state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and evidence of source of funds for the initial contribution (required for the AML/KYC file of the RBE filing and the future Luxembourg bank account)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization as required by the receiving Luxembourg bank on a case-by-case basis; at a minimum, notarized signature and authenticated bank seal

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), particularly Article 906-1 et seq. for the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) as inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013; RCS filing regime and publication obligations under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register and the Annual Accounts of Undertakings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) through the electronic filing window on MyGuichet.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Deed of incorporation (acte de constitution / contrat de société) of the SCSp, executed before a Luxembourg notary or by private writing and submitted to the RCS in the standardized electronic RCS constitution extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital. The SCSp freely defines capital and financing in the partnership agreement; zero capitalization is permitted. If contributions are made, they may be credited to an account in the SCSp's name and blocked until the RCS registration certificate is issued; no statutory escrow or obligatory notarial consignment applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned general partner of [SCSp name] hereby resolves: (1) to ratify the SCSp partnership agreement and to accept the subscription of the initial limited-partner capital commitments as entered in the contribution register; (2) to adopt the registered office at [street address], Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, as the statutory seat and principal place of administration; (3) to appoint [manager name] as managing director (gérant) with sole day-to-day management powers and [signatory name] as deputy bank signatory; and (4) to instruct the gérant to open bank accounts, complete RCS and RBE filings, apply for the business establishment permit for NVOCC freight forwarding, and register the company for VAT and social security. Unanimously adopted and effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name reservation and RCS availability verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS online portal via MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic name reservation request for the proposed SCSp name. Verify the name is not identical or confusingly similar to any registered Luxembourg or European company and that it ends with the mandatory suffix 'SCSp', 'S.C.Sp.' or equivalent. The reservation is valid for the statutory RCS reservation window; proceed to deed drafting only after clearance.
required_dossiers: Passport copy of the general partner or authorized representative
Certificate of incorporation and good standing for any corporate partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on similarity grounds, file a formal contestation with the RCS within 15 days or resubmit alternative distinctive names. Incorporation cannot proceed with a confusingly similar name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg) or RCS-accepted private deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement (statuts/contrat de société) containing corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose limited to NVOCC ocean freight forwarding and logistics, general partner management powers, limited partner rights, profit distribution waterfall, and dissolution terms. Execute as a notarial act where real estate is contributed; otherwise a private deed is permitted, but notarial execution is recommended for bank, client, and registry acceptance.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement / deed of constitution
Passports and proof of residence of all partners and managers
Registered office address and landlord's written consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal or drafting defects, revise and re-execute the deed on the same day. If the RCS later rejects the deed, the partners adopt an amending resolution to correct and re-file the document.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the corporate bank account and capital contribution attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg or EU-licensed credit institution (supervised by the CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an SCSp bank account and, if the partnership agreement provides for paid-in capital, deposit the agreed contributions and obtain a banker's attestation of deposit. Funds may be blocked until presentation of the RCS registration extract. No statutory minimum applies and capital can be zero.
required_dossiers: Passports and addresses of beneficial owners and managers
Brief business plan describing NVOCC operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank makes additional KYC requests, supply a source-of-wealth memorandum and organizational chart. The bank must release funds within 3 business days after receipt of the final RCS extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of the incorporation deed with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – MyGuichet.lu e-filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed constitution deed electronically together with the standardized RCS electronic extract. Attach the partnership agreement, registered office consent, managers' consent letters, and identification documents. Pay the statutory RCS registration fee online. The RCS verifies statutory compliance and issues the Luxembourg registration number.
required_dossiers: Signed constitution deed (notarial or private writing)
Proof of payment of RCS fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (mise en demeure), supply the missing records within 30 days. A refusal may be appealed to the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within 40 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RESA publication and issuance of the RCS registration extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS / Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, the RCS automatically publishes a certified excerpt in the RESA. Legal personality of the SCSp arises from the deed and its RCS registration; the publication grants opposability to third parties after the statutory publication window. The RCS extract serves as conclusive proof of existence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request rectification of inaccurate published data by written application to the RCS; clerical errors are corrected ex officio without additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial owner registration with the RBE
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the RBE declaration within 30 days of RCS registration, identifying every individual holding more than 25% of capital or voting rights, exercising control by other means, or serving as senior managing official. Pay the RBE filing fee electronically.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE rejects the filing for an incomplete ownership chain, submit a corrected declaration with a notarized ownership chart within 10 days. Administrative fines apply only to material failure beyond the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, social security and statistical registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Statec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic VAT registration questionnaire to the AED and obtain a Luxembourg VAT number. Register the managing partner and any employees with the CCSS. Notify Statec for statistical profiling. Note that international ocean freight services may be zero-rated under Article 148(a) of the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, but registration remains mandatory for input VAT recovery and invoicing.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of manager and employees
Bank account details of the SCSp
Registered office lease or ownership title
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AED contests the place of supply or classification of freight services, submit transport contracts, bills of lading, and container manifests. Written objections must be filed within 1 month of any proposed adjustment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale de l'industrie, des PME et de l'entrepreneuriat (Ministry of the Economy, Directorate-General for Industry, SMEs and Entrepreneurship) through the MyGuichet.lu 'Autorisation d'établissement' channel; supplementary transport-intermediary clearance with the Ministère de la Mobilité et des Travaux publics where the NVOCC contracts carriage in its own name.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) for 'transport and logistics intermediaries / freight forwarding' under the amended Law of 2 September 2011, supplemented, where applicable, by a freight-forwarding intermediary declaration (déclaration de commissionnaire de transport) for own-name contracting carrier activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement – Ministry of Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class C / non-classified establishment. Office-only NVOCC premises fall below the mandatory EIA screening thresholds of the amended Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; no full EIA report is required. A simplified registration as a producer of hazardous waste may apply under the Law of 21 March 2012 if the office or warehouse generates regulated waste.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic-strength wastewater only, discharging to municipal sewers under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 December 1990 on wastewater; negligible VOC or industrial air emissions; packaging waste and WEEE must be collected through certified waste collectors pursuant to the amended Law of 21 March 2012 and applicable extended producer responsibility decrees.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety conformity attestation (attestation de sécurité incendie) issued by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) for offices and any bonded storage; workplace compliance inspection by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) covering emergency exits, work equipment, first aid, and health-and-safety documentation; structural stability and load-bearing records to be maintained by the registered-office owner and presented upon ITM audit.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and indirect taxes; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct income taxes. Both authorities operate through the unified MyGuichet.lu digital gateway (eTVA, e-CDF); official portals: guichet.lu, impotsdirects.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident NVOCC must first obtain the Luxembourg national business number (matricule) via registration of the SCSp with the Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu) where a local establishment exists; it then files VAT Form 645 ('Demande d'immatriculation à la TVA') with the AEDT through MyGuichet.lu, attaching the constitutive deed, RCS extract, proof of Luxembourg place of management, and identity of the authorised representative. The AEDT issues the Luxembourg VAT identification number (format 'LU' + 8 digits) within approximately 3-6 weeks. Where the foreign NVOCC supplies only B2B services to Luxembourg recipients, the recipient self-assesses VAT under the reverse-charge mechanism and no local VAT ID is mandatory; a foreign supplier seeking input-VAT refunds may use the EU e-VAT refund portal without creating a Luxembourg VAT registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. The SCSp is statutorily fiscally transparent and has no legal personality: it is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) or net wealth tax; each partner is taxed personally on their allocable share of profits, with non-resident partners taxable only where the SCSp constitutes a Luxembourg permanent establishment for them (normally present for an SCSp managed and controlled from Luxembourg). The SCSp enterprise remains the assessment unit for municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) and is treated as an independent taxable person for VAT and customs purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Luxembourg; transparent treatment is mandatory for the SCSp. Available mechanisms include: advance tax rulings from the ACD confirming fiscal transparency and profit allocation; the Article 57 VAT small-business franchise (opt-in to normal VAT taxation); VAT grouping (assujetti unique) with Luxembourg affiliates; and fiscal year alignment. Anti-hybrid rules (Article 168ter/168quater LIR implementing ATAD 2) restrict deduction/non-inclusion mismatches where a foreign partner treats the SCSp as an opaque entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax ('TVA') harmonised with EU Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold applies to Luxembourg-established taxable persons: VAT registration is mandatory from the first taxable transaction. The Article 57 small-business exemption applies only up to EUR 35,000 of annual taxable turnover (taxpayer may opt into normal taxation). Non-resident NVOCCs face no mandatory registration threshold for B2B services (reverse charge applies); registration is triggered by intra-Community acquisitions of goods or by B2C supplies performed within Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2G e-invoicing is mandatory: suppliers to Luxembourg public entities must transmit invoices via the PEPPOL network in EN 16931 / PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0 format; paper or PDF invoices are unacceptable in public procurement. There is no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping for B2B invoices; compliance rests on standard Article 226 invoice data, electronic VAT returns (eTVA via MyGuichet.lu), European Sales List filings, and periodic submission of the Luxembourg SAF-T-LV XML audit file by selected VAT payers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% exemption-with-credit applies to international maritime transport of goods and to NVOCC brokerage, ocean freight, container handling and customs-clearance services directly linked to goods entering or leaving the EU (Article 148(a)/(d) of EU Directive 2006/112/EC; Articles 53 et seq. of the amended Luxembourg VAT law). Eligibility requires a direct contractual and economic link between the service and a voyage on an ocean-going vessel with a port of loading and a port of discharge inside and outside the EU; transportation organised by the NVOCC as principal (contracting carrier) qualifies in full, whereas purely domestic agency or commission components performed solely within Luxembourg are taxable at 17%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration: Export Accompanying Document / MRN generated in the EU Automated Export System evidencing lodging and physical exit of the goods
Bill of Lading: ocean Master/Through Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill in the name of the shipper/NVOCC and the foreign consignee, confirming the cross-border port-to-port route
Inward Remittance Certificate: bank SWIFT MT103 or credit advice proving receipt of the foreign currency payment from the overseas counterparty within the 180-day benchmark
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg imposes no statutory exchange-control repatriation deadline; 180 days is the customary banking and customs documentary benchmark for matching export proceeds. The AEDT may reassess zero-rated exports within 5 years, extended to 10 years for fraudulent or incomplete files; failure to produce the required documentation triggers recapture of the 17% VAT, a 10% statutory surcharge (majoration) and monthly late-payment interest of 0.6%. Forged Bills of Lading, false customs declarations or orchestrated round-tripping constitute VAT fraud, punishable by criminal fines and imprisonment with OLAF coordination in cross-border cases; the general anti-abuse rule also permits retrospective disregard of artificial freight-route or invoice-chain structures.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting as the national central bank under the European System of Central Banks (ESCB); the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) exercises licensing and prudential supervision over Luxembourg credit institutions and payment/electronic money institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg operates within the eurozone under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union; the euro (EUR) is fully convertible across both current and capital account transactions, with no approval or surrender requirements for non-resident partners, no foreign exchange rationing, and no separate domestic FX convertibility regime. Profit remittances by an SCSp to non-resident partners are legally free of exchange-control restrictions, subject only to standard AML/KYC verification, tax compliance under the Luxembourg tax code, and, where applicable, withholding tax characterization under double tax treaties. For a NVOCC freight forwarding operation, payments to non-EU carriers, port authorities, and service providers are generally unrestricted, but must be properly documented to satisfy EU anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing (AML/CTF) obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender obligation exists under Luxembourg law. Because Luxembourg is a eurozone member and has fully liberalized capital movements under EU Directive 88/361/EEC and Articles 63-66 TFEU, ocean freight forwarding/NVOCC export-entitlement receivables may be retained in EUR or any freely convertible currency. No mandatory conversion ratio or repatriation timeline applies. Nevertheless, the SCSp must observe EU statistical reporting thresholds imposed by the BCL for cross-border transactions and positions (positive and negative) exceeding EUR 12,500 per calendar month, with consolidated reporting required for intra-EU and extra-EU movements through the BCL's direct reporting system.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Luxembourg-licensed fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) operating under CSSF authorization and PSD2 are viable for low-volume operational treasury functions of the SCSp, such as vendor payments and travel expenses, with a Medium feasibility rating for this NVOCC business. Offshore digital EMIs not established in the EEA or not licensed by the CSSF have Limited viability due to (i) lack of access to Target2 payment systems, (ii) restrictions in correspondent banking relationships, (iii) inability to issue commercial letters of credit, and (iv) stricter enhanced due diligence requirements imposed on SCSp partnerships by Luxembourg banks. The SCSp should rely on onshore tier-1 banks for core clearing, FX, and trade finance rails, using EMIs only as secondary fee-management tools.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg's AML/CTF framework under the law of 12 November 2004 (as amended) and CSSF regulations do not universally mandate physical presence, but in practice most tier-1 banks require at least one physical interview for SCSp entities that have no substantive local office and whose partners are non-resident. Remote onboarding may be permitted for fully digital banks or EMIs using qualified electronic identification, but under Luxembourg know-your-customer rules, directors and general partners must submit notarized and apostilled identification, updated corporate registers, and a certified copy of the SCSp partnership agreement. For an NVOCC freight forwarder, the bank will normally require a signed confirmation of beneficial ownership, an explanation of the ownership chain, and a physical meeting with the SCSp's authorized manager as an enhanced-due-diligence condition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp with zero minimum capital, no local substance, and offshore ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg partnership agreement (contrat de société) with certified translation; register of beneficial owners maintained under Luxembourg law; notarized UBO passport copies; corporate organizational structure and rationale for using an SCSp in a freight forwarding brokerage; evidence of commercial substance including sub-charter contracts, office lease/co-working agreement, and employment or outsourcing proof.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transactional velocity in payments to non-EU carriers, ports, and freight suppliers without standard invoices
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly executed NVOCC contracts with ocean carriers; bills of lading and house bills of lading; commercial invoices; port tariff schedules; payment ledger matching order-to-cash and procure-to-pay flows; annual audited financial statements or management accounts; carrier/supplier KYC files.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential mismatch between stated ISIC 5229 forwarding activity and rerouted payments to sanctioned territories
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening and sanctions compliance policy aligned with EU/UN sanctions lists; CDD file of each counterparty and beneficial owner; consolidated cargo routing documents; customs declarations and EU TAXUD transit records; evidence of licensed NVOCC status and freight forwarder liability insurance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of partner loans or quasi-equity injections into the SCSp as the main capital source
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Partnership agreement clauses authorizing capital contributions and shareholder/partner advances; source-of-funds statements for all contributing partners; signed loan agreements with defined maturity and interest; bank statements showing clearing of partner funds through regulated financial institutions; tax opinion on debt-equity characterization under Luxembourg tax law.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the SCSp must be routed by wire through a correspondent bank to the Luxembourg resident account held at a BIL, BGL BNP Paribas, or Société Générale Bank & Trust. The remitter must use SWIFT MT103 with the payment purpose code clearly indicating either a direct capital contribution (e.g., 'C1 — Equity capital' under Luxembourg/BCL BoP coding) or a partner loan ('C4 — Intercompany financing'); the receiving bank will require the SCSp's legal name, UBO identification, and copy of the executed partnership agreement. Verification includes BCL monthly external position reporting if aggregated flows exceed EUR 12,500, completion of the bank's internal source-of-funds form, and confirmation of the economic substance behind the contribution to prevent re-characterization as a loan for tax, AML, or thin capitalization purposes. Capital call notices must reference the SCSp's partnership agreement and identify the partner, contribution date, and currency.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for NVOCC trade settlements operate through the standard international payment rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for freight payments, port fees, trucking charges, and customs duties, using ISO 20022-structured remittance information and the correct tariff/industry purpose codes (e.g., BOPS 'ITR' transportation codes); (ii) commercial letters of credit (L/C) issued by the Luxembourg bank at the request of the SCSp's client for ocean freight pre-financing, using UCP 600 rules, with freight forwarder documents of title such as the master bill of lading and forwarders' certificate of receipt; and (iii) ACH direct debits for low-value domestic EU disbursements via SEPA infrastructure. The SCSp must maintain full documentary archives for each rail, including the underlying invoice, bill of lading, and proof of payment, to satisfy the bank's transactional monitoring and CSSF/Wolfsberg group expectations for freight forwarding accounts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD foreign exchange forwards on a delivery or cash-settlement basis, executed under ISDA or local master agreement, when tied to genuine freight invoicing streams.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) against convertible emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, BRL) where underlying trade does not permit physical delivery due to local FX controls, provided the NDF counterparty is a licensed bank and the trade is economically grounded in anticipated freight revenues.
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/GBP) for the re-alignment of cash flows from long-term carrier contracts and charter-party agreements, used purely for hedging rather than speculative leverage.
OTC currency options (EUR call/USD put) purchased to protect against adverse USD appreciation in the context of ocean freight payable quotes, not for trading revenue.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of RCS core registration data (Confirmation annuelle des données du RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation window fixed by LBR; for entities on a calendar year, confirmation typically required between 1 January and 31 March following the confirmation reference date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late confirmation triggers a penalty of up to EUR 2,500 per overdue item; continued non-compliance may lead to administrative strike-off from RCS after formal notice and a 30-day cure period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and annual accounts deposit (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar financial year: approval by partners within 6 months of year-end (by 30 June); deposit with RCS within 1 month of approval, with absolute deadline of 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unlimited liability partners and SCSp managers are jointly liable for unpaid taxes; court fine up to EUR 10,000 plus publication penalty judgment; failure to file for two consecutive years can trigger compulsory liquidation or administrative strike-off under the amended Law of 10 August 1915.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO register data update or confirmation (RBE - Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Beneficial Ownership Register (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual filing date; confirmation performed each time a relevant event occurs and periodically when the annual RCS confirmation shows UBO data unchanged; all changes filed within 1 month of occurrence.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 for non-declaration of beneficial ownership under Article 3 of the Law of 13 January 2019; RBE access can be blocked and default interest accrues on tax assessment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) for Luxembourg SCSp if at least two of the following thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive years: total balance sheet EUR 4.4m (approx. USD 4.8m); net turnover EUR 8.8m (approx. USD 9.6m); average full-time employees 50. Audit also required earlier if the SCSp is the parent of a group preparing consolidated accounts or if required by the partnership agreement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; IFRS as adopted by the EU mandatory for consolidated accounts but optional for individual SCSp accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: SCSp is pass-through for Luxembourg tax and not itself subject to corporate income tax; however, the general partner and the NVOCC service provider must annually reconcile the register of general partners and transferees. Any transfer of partnership interest must be evidenced by notarized or private deed and notified to the RBE within 1 month; changes take effect against third parties only after registration and publication in the RCS.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors / General Partner registry

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 3,300 - USD 8,700 per year for Luxembourg registered office and licensed agent services for an SCSp NVOCC vehicle
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,600 - USD 26,000 per annual statutory audit, depending on asset volumes, partner complexity and whether the ocean freight forwarding/NVOCC business requires consolidated-group deliverables

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City aggregate: 17% CIT + 7% unemployment surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption (100% on qualifying dividends, 80% on capital gains); 80% IP box exemption on qualifying IP income; 20% R&D super-deduction; Notional Interest Deduction (NID) for equity; possibility of so-called 'exempt income from transfer of shares' under Luxembourg law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 210 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des sociétés de personnes) submitted electronically via MyGuichet.lu / ACD e-Filing space
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within six months of the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities, by 30 June of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification: legal form (SCSp), VAT or national business register number, Y-number (RCS), address of registered office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide correct Y-number (RCS Luxembourg) and designate the representative partner's tax jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use full dates (DD/MM/YYYY). A short first tax period incurs annualised assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit (bénéfice commercial courant) as determined under Luxembourg GAAP
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Partners must add back any non-deductible or disallowed expenses; attach partner allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs: fines, taxes not deductible, excessive interest, entertainment expenses, depreciation reserves
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filing must list all items separately with supporting documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: participation exemption, IP box deduction, R&D super-deduction, tax loss carryforwards used
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For transparent SCSp, any tax adjustments are made at partner level; do not claim entity-level exemptions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocable taxable income share per partner (quota) according to partnership agreement and capital contributions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide full name, tax residence, and quote of each partner; for corporate partners, include their corporate tax number.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine of up to EUR 5,000, automatic 10% increase of assessed tax, and late-payment interest of 0.6% per month on overdue amounts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic; 0% under Luxembourg participation exemption when corporate partner holds at least 10% and satisfies holding period/there is no main motive to avoid taxation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain reduced withholding tax under a DTA, the beneficial owner (non-resident partner) must submit a current Luxembourg tax residence certificate (TRC) to the withholding agent via the ACD's withholding tax relief procedure, and where applicable, file the standard 'Demande de remboursement' (Form 22) or request relief at source before the date of distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% domestic for patent royalties; 0% for most non-patent royalties; treaty rates can reduce the 10% rate. Interest: 0% domestic WHT, but debt equity ratio must respect thin capitalization rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master file required for MNE groups with consolidated revenue ≥ EUR 750 million. Local file required only if the Luxembourg entity engages in intercompany transactions where the total value exceeds EUR 100 million per fiscal year (threshold applied to both inbound and outbound transactions).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: SCSp must have real economic substance (own office, employees, management decisions, bank accounts in Luxembourg) to benefit from treaty access and avoid being characterized as a self-complacent shell enterprise. The Luxembourg ACD applies substance over form and may disregard the partnership under GAAR anti-abuse provisions, especially if the entity is managed/administered abroad.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Detailing deliberately underreported NVOCC ocean freight income, cash collection, or overstatement of deductions such as logistics costs, cartage, and port handling fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to EUR 1 million or twice the evaded tax, and imprisonment up to 10 years; civil restitution plus default interest of 0.6% per month; loss of claim to treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or managing partners are jointly liable to pay evaded taxes, may be subject to travel bans and seizure of assets, and in aggravated cases imprisonment for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SCSp is managed from abroad, has no commercial justification, maintains a mailbox address only, and operates as a pass-through conduit for NVOCC bookings without active conduct of freight forwarding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of partnership, re-characterization of profits, retroactive tax assessment including 10% increase, and denial of DTA access; administrative fines up to EUR 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for corporate taxes, interest, and fines; possible prohibition on managing a company in Luxembourg for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform client due diligence (Know-Your-Customer) or intentionally ignoring suspicious money laundering through invoice payments for ocean transportation or payment rails (Swift Wire / ACH Direct).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial penalties up to EUR 5 million for legal entities and up to EUR 1 million for directors under the 2004 AML law; seizure of illicit commissions; criminal imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Criminal liability as beneficial owner; personal fines; deportation for non-EU directors; revocation of supervisory mandates throughout European Economic Area.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare contemporaneous Local File/Master File within statutory deadline, or carrying out intercompany transactions with offshore related parties without adequate mark-up.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 10% of the profit adjustment, minimum EUR 5,000; increase of taxable base; interest at 0.6% per month; possible disallowance of deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who fail to maintain proper transfer pricing documentation are collectively liable for the penalty when negligent; personal fines up to EUR 50,000 may be imposed.
